subject: Measurement invariance of intensive longitudinal data

messages.author: b59994071deff2fe
messages.subject: Measurement invariance of intensive longitudinal data
parts:
Hi all

I have a dataset where each participant has completed a 6 item measure for 7 days at each of three different time points. Ie:

Week x: Day 1 - 7

Week y: Day 1 - 7

Week z: Day 1 - 7

The measurement model of the items is a unidimensional structure. Could someone point me towards an example of how to assess measurement invariance between the three timepoints (i.e. Week x,y and z). The reason that the level "week" is important is because we want to see whether, when participants have a break from the questionnaire between weeks, if this impacts the assumed invariance.

I was looking at multilevel SEM (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/multilevel.html) but here I think I have an additional level of clustering (i.e. days nested within weeks nested within participants). I am not sure that this can be handled in Lavaan, and I may need to go to Mplus if not. 

Thanks in advance for the help,

Pip

messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance of intensive longitudinal data
parts: Could someone point me towards an example of how to assess measurement invariance between the three timepoints (i.e. Week x,y and z)

https://jeroendmulder.github.io/RI-CLPM/lavaan.html#Ext_3:_multiple_indicator

You would need invariance across all 21 timepoints (7 days in each of 3 waves).

I was looking at multilevel SEM (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/multilevel.html) but here I think I have an additional level of clustering (i.e. days nested within weeks nested within participants). I am not sure that this can be handled in Lavaan, and I may need to go to Mplus if not.

It depends on your research question.  What was the purpose of gathering 7 days of data on each wave?  If that is just noise around an average for that time, you could treat subjects as clusters (7 observations each, in long format), with the 3 waves handled in wide format (different variables, like longitudinal CFA usually is fit).  Just an example, not sure if it maps onto your study design or RQ.
